title: helm-annotation-dependency-templates-and-init-gate-values
author: Ethan Schultz
description:
Motivation: Private installs occasionally fail when init hooks run out-of-order across tenant slices in constrained clusters (observed in multiple customer upgrades). Existing hook sequencing is static and tied to job creation order; operators asked for a lightweight mechanism to express hook inter-dependencies and a values-driven gate that prevents prewarm/pvc claims from racing. This PR adds a terse annotation-based dependency template for Helm hook jobs and a new values schema section `initGates` that enables cluster- or tenant-scoped gating policies. Key goals: 1) allow chart consumers to express 'wait-for:<hook-id>' dependencies on hooks without adding a separate controller; 2) provide a declarative values surface to enable cautious prewarm/pvc claim ordering; 3) keep default behavior unchanged for existing installs.

What this PR contains (summary): - New templating helper `hook.dependencies.tpl` that resolves 'helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on' annotations into an init container check loop. - values.schema.json extended with `initGates` schema (max 3 gate profiles, optional gating TTLs, and per-tenant overrides). - Updated `templates/init-job.yaml` and `templates/tenant-seed-job.yaml` to consume the helper and short-circuit job start until dependencies are satisfied (idempotent wait loop). - Added `templates/_helpers.tpl` helpers to render safe annotation keys and gate labels. - README and docs/upgrade-notes describing migration, toggles, and troubleshooting steps. - Unit tests for helper rendering and a small e2e scenario (helm chart template tests) to cover gated startup.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by infra and installability team (ENG-10342) - [x] Schema validated against Helm lint - [x] Unit tests added for template helpers - [x] Integration e2e rerun to validate gating in minimal k8s - [x] Docs and upgrade notes added - [x] Backwards-compatible defaults preserved

How the annotation-based dependency works (illustrative snippet): "annotations:\n  helm.redwood.ai/hook-id: tenant-seed\n  helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on: tenant-db-init,prewarm-claim"\nThe helper expands into an init container that polls for a ConfigMap-based token created by the referenced hooks. The referenced hook jobs, when successful, write a small stamped ConfigMap (name derived from hook-id) that unblocks dependents. This is intentionally light-weight and uses only Kubernetes primitives (ConfigMap + owner references) to avoid adding new controllers.

Values surface (new section): "initGates": {"profiles": [{"name":"conservative","maxParallel":2,"pvcClaimWaitSeconds":45}],"defaultProfile":"conservative","tenantOverrides": {"tenant-a":"aggressive"}}\nDefault is empty and has no gating; cluster operators can opt-in via values or use a global profile in the operator overlay.

Migration and rollout notes: - Default chart behavior is unchanged unless `initGates` is set or hooks annotate `helm.redwood.ai/hook-depends-on`. - For upgrades where existing hooks assume old ordering, enable the gating profile in a staged rollout (canary tenants first). - For air-gapped/private installs, the dependency mechanism uses in-cluster ConfigMaps and does not require external network access. - We ship an `upgrade-notes.md` section that calls out a 5-step canary process.

Security considerations: created ConfigMaps contain only small opaque tokens; we added RBAC snippets so install roles can create/read the token ConfigMaps and are namespaced-scoped by default. Operators who prefer stricter scopes can bind a patch to limit access.

Testing: - unit: template rendering tests (helm template assertions) - integration: scripted helm install/upgrade in KinD with two tenant namespaces showing gated ordering - e2e: flake observed on CI once; reran e2e, green. CI logs reference: build/helm-lint, test/templates, kind-integration (rerun), docs-check.

review_thread:
Maya Patel (reviewer): Can we avoid ConfigMaps and use annotations on Jobs? Reason: ConfigMap churn in very large clusters can be noisy.
Ethan Schultz (author): We considered annotations; however Jobs disappear on completion and we need a stable object to signal across namespaces and ensure idempotence. ConfigMaps are tiny and namespaced; we limited lifecycle and added TTL semantics.
Lina Ortega (reviewer): Please add explicit RBAC to values so operators can opt into least-privileged roles.
Ethan Schultz: Added a `rbacTokenConfig` toggle in values and documented the minimal Role/RoleBinding required.
Harold Kim (approver): Verified templates in KinD and the gating profile worked as expected for 2 tenant namespaces. Approving with suggestion to monitor configmap count in monitoring dashboards post-rollout.
Merge-bot: CI passed after re-run of kind-integration; merging via squash.
release_notes: Add annotation-driven hook dependencies and optional init gating profiles for private installs. Operators can opt-in via `initGates` values. Backwards compatible unless enabled. See charts/private/docs/upgrade-notes.md for canary checklist and troubleshooting steps.
notes_for_ops: Enable by setting charts.private.initGates.defaultProfile and apply incrementally. Watch for ConfigMap growth under namespace scope and monitor `helm_init_gate_unblocked_total` (added metric) to observe gating behavior.
testing_instructions:
1) helm template to validate rendering: `helm template . -f values.yaml`
2) install in a test namespace with initGates set to conservative profile
3) create two tenant namespaces and run tenant seeding; observe that dependent hooks wait until their referenced tokens are present
4) rollback: revert values or remove hook annotations; old behavior restored immediately
notes: This PR intentionally avoids a new controller to keep the installer footprint small. If we see widespread demand for cross-namespace orchestration we can iterate with an opt-in controller in a follow-up PR.
